clue.text: 100.000 rupees, say, deposited in soldier's bank for protection

indicators.note: money deposited in an account sits inside it, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier; the possessive adds S
a lac (lakh) is a hundred thousand, typically of rupees; 'say' marks rupees as just an example

explanation.surface: A soldier pays a large sum of rupees into his bank to keep it safe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' looks financial, sitting next to 'deposited' and rupees, but it is an earthwork. The OCR shows a point where the page has the comma of 100,000.
explanation.definitionFit: A glacis is the sloping earthen embankment in front of a fortification, built to expose attackers and shield defenders.

clue.text: Illegally transfer several articles from abroad

parts.note: la is a French definite article; 'several' asks for more than one foreign article
un is a French indefinite article
der is a German definite article

explanation.surface: Smuggling a number of goods into the country from overseas.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Several' tells you to string together more than one foreign word for 'the' or 'a'.
explanation.definitionFit: To launder money is to move illicit funds through legitimate channels to disguise where they came from.

clue.text: Associates in business given short change

parts.note: Co is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: to change something is to alter its form, so these letters are reordered

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Business partners handed too little money back at the till.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short change' looks like a single phrase about cheating, but 'short' is the fodder and 'change' the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Cohorts are companions or supporters, people who keep company with someone.

clue.text: Do climb up crack

parts.note: to shin up is to climb using arms and legs
a wisecrack or gibe, a dig at someone

explanation.surface: An instruction to clamber up a fissure in a rock face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Do' reads as a verb, but it is the noun meaning a party.
explanation.definitionFit: A shindig is an informal word for a lively party or celebration, as is a do.

clue.text: One police force operating within the law — that's taken for granted

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one
the Military Police
lawful, permitted by law

explanation.surface: A police force acting legally is something the public assumes as a matter of course.
explanation.definitionFit: Something implicit is understood or assumed without being stated outright, which is what goes unquestioned.

clue.text: Thin gloom could be dispelled in this

definitions.text: Thin gloom could be dispelled in this

indicators.note: dispelling scatters something, so these letters are scattered and regrouped

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A faint darkness lifts under a night sky's pale light.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the wordplay and the definition: the light that relieves a weak darkness.
explanation.definitionFit: Light from the moon is exactly what eases a faint night-time darkness.

clue.text: As a rule, women going crazy over right gardening equipment

parts.note: a law is a rule

indicators.note: going crazy means losing order, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: fodder taken as written
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Women typically go wild about the proper tool for the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As a' is padding that makes the surface read as 'as a rule', meaning generally; only 'rule' gives letters. In a down clue 'over' puts the earlier pieces above R.
explanation.definitionFit: A lawnmower is the machine used to cut grass, a standard piece of garden kit.

clue.text: Bed — I will get one immediately after the dance

parts.note: a cot is a small bed
the contraction I'll
the Roman numeral for one
on as in 'on arrival', at once after

explanation.surface: Someone vows to go straight to bed once the ball is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Immediately after' reads as timing for the whole sentence but supplies a small word itself.
explanation.definitionFit: The cotillion was a lively French-origin ballroom dance for couples, popular in the eighteenth century.

clue.text: Ottoman's topped by this ornamental ropework

definitions.meaning: first meaning, cryptic: the head of a Turkish subject sits on top of him

explanation.walkthrough: An Ottoman here is a Turk, not the footstool the surface suggests; what tops a Turk is his head.
explanation.definitionFit: A Turk's head is a decorative knot woven round a rope or rail, resembling a turban.

clue.text: Drunk? Turn red, not black

indicators.note: 'not black' asks for the letter standing for black to be left out

parts.note: to go red in the face
B is the pencil-grade abbreviation for black

explanation.surface: Is someone tipsy? Their face flushes, though it is not a black mood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' reads as an adjective, but the answer is the slang noun for a heavy drinker.
explanation.definitionFit: A lush is informal slang for a habitual heavy drinker, an alcoholic person.

clue.text: Where eggs may be cooked for it

definitions.meaning: literal meaning: in a pan of boiling liquid
second meaning: in trouble, as in 'you'll be for it'

explanation.walkthrough: 'For it' is British slang for being due a telling-off or punishment.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is both a literal place to boil eggs and an idiom for being in serious trouble.

clue.text: A party Socialist was devoted to

parts.note: taken as written
a do is a party or celebration
red is the colour of the left, so a Red is a socialist

explanation.surface: Someone who loyally served a left-wing party in their younger days.
explanation.definitionFit: To have adored someone is to have loved them deeply, the same as having been devoted to them.

clue.text: Positive about animal being put down

definitions.note: plural noun answer for a mass noun: soft feathers

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so one piece wraps round the other

parts.note: the plus sign is the positive sign
a mule is a horse-donkey cross

explanation.surface: Someone is sure about an animal having to be humanely destroyed by the vet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put down' suggests putting an animal to sleep, but 'down' alone is the definition: fluffy feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: Plumules are the small soft feathers of a bird, collectively its down.

clue.text: Force to join crowd and go north of the border

parts.note: a press is a dense crowd or throng
gang is the Scots word for go; north of the border means in Scotland

explanation.surface: Someone is pressured to join a throng and travel up into Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' is Scotland, whose dialect uses 'gang' for 'go'.
explanation.definitionFit: To press-gang is to coerce someone into service, as navy crews once seized men to serve at sea.

clue.text: Get over to vote

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to communicate an idea successfully
second meaning, split into three words: mark an X on a ballot paper

explanation.surface: Persuade someone to go and cast their ballot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as three words, the phrase describes marking an X, which is how British voters fill in a ballot.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something across is to convey it clearly; marking an X is the act of voting.

clue.text: He and I could be so described

definitions.text: He and I could be so described

parts.note: surface reading: two people, a man and the speaker; setter's reading: the chemical symbols for helium and iodine

explanation.surface: Someone describing themselves and a male friend.
explanation.walkthrough: The pronouns are chemical symbols; both substances appear in the periodic table.
explanation.definitionFit: Helium and iodine are chemical elements, so the adjective relating to elements fits them.

clue.text: Yearns to be beset by bribes and slush

indicators.note: being beset means being surrounded on all sides, so one piece is enclosed

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or buy off
pines means longs or yearns

explanation.surface: Someone longing for things is surrounded by backhanders and melting snow.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slush' suggests half-melted snow, but here it means mawkish sentimentality.
explanation.definitionFit: Soppiness is excessive sentimentality, the cloying quality called slush or mush.

clue.text: Star group firmly attached to rock

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a constellation in the northern sky
second meaning: the princess of Greek myth chained to a sea cliff

explanation.surface: A band of celebrities holds firmly to rock music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Star group' and 'rock' suggest a band and its music; the clue is about astronomy and myth.
explanation.definitionFit: The constellation is named after the mythical princess who was chained to a rock as an offering to a sea monster.

clue.text: Record sound acoustically

indicators.note: acoustics concern hearing, so the word is taken as heard rather than as spelt

parts.note: sound in the sense of correct, valid

explanation.surface: An engineer is told to capture audio in good acoustic conditions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Record sound' looks like a studio instruction, but 'sound' means correct here.
explanation.definitionFit: To write something down is to record it in permanent written form.

clue.text: Port abandoned by an idiot

indicators.note: the port's name is left by the following word, which drops away from it

parts.note: the Belgian port
taken as written

explanation.surface: A harbour town has been deserted by some fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Twerp is an informal insult for a silly or contemptible person, a fool.

clue.text: Unseated — in fact, unseated after losing weight

indicators.note: 'in' places the trimmed word inside the word for fact

parts.note: deed as in 'in deed', a fact or actual act

indicators.note: a letter is shed from the second 'unseated' word, as one sheds pounds

parts.note: as a rider thrown by a horse
W is the abbreviation for weight

explanation.surface: A deposed ruler, literally thrown from the saddle, having slimmed down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In fact' reads as a filler phrase, but 'in' is the container signal and 'fact' gives DEED.
explanation.definitionFit: A dethroned monarch has been removed from power, unseated from their throne.

clue.text: Unscrupulous character hurtles madly around

indicators.note: moving madly around is chaotic, so the word's letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A shady crook races about at reckless speed.
explanation.definitionFit: A hustler is a swindler or con artist who makes money by dishonest, aggressive means.

clue.text: Casual worker not working at first

indicators.note: 'at first' puts the idle description in front, ahead of the labourer

parts.note: off as in off duty or switched off
a hand is a manual worker, as a farmhand

explanation.surface: A temporary employee who was idle at the start of the shift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Casual worker' reads as one phrase for a temp, but 'Casual' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Offhand describes a careless, nonchalant manner, which is to say casual.

clue.text: In road, steep climbs going on for ever

indicators.note: in a down entry, climbing means going upward, so the letters read bottom to top
'In' places the soaking word inside the word for a road

parts.note: a lane is a narrow road
to ret is to soak flax in water, so steep

explanation.surface: A steep hill on a road that seems to climb forever.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steep' looks like an adjective for a hill; it is the verb meaning soak, and RET is that verb in flax processing.
explanation.definitionFit: Eternal means lasting without end, continuing for all time.

clue.text: Poor director to whom money is owing

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for 'one to whom money is owing'

indicators.note: something poor is in bad shape, so the following word is in disorder

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: A struggling company boss who is still owed money.
explanation.definitionFit: A creditor is a person or firm that has lent money and is waiting to be repaid by a debtor.

clue.text: Son frequently exhibiting temper

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for son
a direct synonym

explanation.surface: A boy who regularly throws tantrums.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Temper' reads as a noun, a bad mood; it is the verb meaning to moderate.
explanation.definitionFit: To soften something is to make it less harsh, which is to temper or tone it down.

clue.text: Above board that's not uneven

explanation.surface: A flat surface sitting over a plank.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means honest and genuine, while literally it describes something lying perfectly flat.

clue.text: Composer learned when guided around

indicators.note: 'around' also tells us to turn the remaining letters about into a new order
the word for guided is to be found and stripped from the outside of the word learned

parts.note: taken as written
led means guided; it wraps round the other letters in learned

explanation.surface: A composer who picked up his craft by being shown the ropes.
explanation.walkthrough: LEARNED is L-EARN-ED, the word for guided placed around EARN; taking that away leaves EARN to be rearranged. Thomas Arne wrote Rule, Britannia!
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Arne was an eighteenth-century English composer, best known for the patriotic song Rule, Britannia!

clue.text: Drummer in US takes drink aboard ship with crew

indicators.note: a ship that takes something on holds it, so the drink goes inside the vessel
being aboard means being on and within a vessel, enclosed by it

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a type of beer
to man a vessel is to crew it

explanation.surface: An American percussionist drinks on board a ship among the crew.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage a drummer is a travelling salesman, one who drums up trade.
explanation.definitionFit: Drummer is old American slang for a commercial traveller who drums up business for a firm.

clue.text: Put out about extremely delayed puzzle

indicators.note: 'about' means surrounding, so the annoyance word goes round the selected letters

parts.note: to annoy, to put someone out

indicators.note: 'extremely' points to the extremities, the first and last letters of the next word

parts.note: the first and last letters of delayed

explanation.surface: Someone is annoyed by a puzzle that arrived very late.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put out' could mean extinguished; here it means annoyed.
explanation.definitionFit: A riddle is a puzzling question or conundrum posed as a test of wit.
